lead.headline: A record September for Indian auto retail, a rate hike, and a margin squeeze for capital goods
lead.dek: FADA's September print is the strongest ever but flattered by a GST-distorted base. EVs set fresh highs, the RBI turned hawkish, and Q2 previews flag soft ex-L&T order inflows with commodity costs biting.

ticker.text: RBI hikes repo 25 bps to 5.50%; stance shifts to 'calibrated tightening' (4–2 vote)
FADA: Sep-26 retail at record 25.37 lakh units, +31.8% YoY on a GST-distorted base
India EV retail hits all-time high of ~3.34 lakh units in September; e-4W record 36,010
MoD signs ₹661.5 cr contract with BrahMos Aerospace for Navy fire-control systems and launchers
Q2FY27 preview: ex-L&T capital goods inflows seen ~₹35,000 cr, down ~10% YoY

ev.headline: India EV retail sets an all-time monthly high in September
ev.summary: Vahan data shows 3,33,571 EVs registered in September, up from 3,02,746 in August. Electric four-wheelers hit a record 36,010 units, with penetration rising to 8.5% for cars and 11.6% for two-wheelers. Tata Motors still leads e-4W with over 41% share, ahead of Mahindra and JSW MG; TVS, Bajaj and Ather lead e-2W.
ev.whyItMatters: Double-digit 2W penetration and a fast-rising 4W share strengthen the case for cell, battery-pack and charging capex, and keep consolidation among sub-scale e-2W players on the agenda.

ev.headline: Tesla Q3 deliveries beat consensus, but energy storage disappoints
ev.summary: Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026 against a company-compiled consensus of 461,974, down 2.1% YoY but up 1.3% QoQ. Deliveries exceeded production by about 22,000 units, implying an inventory drawdown. Storage deployments of 13.7 GWh fell short of the ~15.9 GWh expected.
ev.whyItMatters: Flat global volumes from the category leader are a useful reference point when benchmarking growth assumptions and multiples for listed Indian EV names.

autos.headline: FADA: best-ever September for auto retail, but read the base effect
autos.summary: Retail sales reached 25,36,920 units, up 31.82% YoY and 4.69% MoM. Two-wheelers rose 33%, PVs 32% and CVs 38%, with CVs crossing one lakh in a September for the first time. H1 FY27 retail is up 20.77%. FADA cautions that September 2025 was depressed by buyers deferring purchases ahead of GST 2.0 and points to roughly 17% underlying growth.
autos.whyItMatters: Normalise for the base before using September in comps or run-rates. Dealer sentiment for Oct–Dec is constructive (78% expect growth), which supports festive-quarter volume estimates.

autos.headline: Mahindra overtakes Tata for #2 in PV retail by 89 units
autos.summary: Maruti Suzuki held 39.59% share (1,69,132 units). Mahindra (57,343) edged Tata (57,254) for second, with Hyundai fourth at 11.75%. Kia posted the fastest YoY growth in the top ten on the new Seltos. Petrol regained a slim lead (41.27%) over CNG, hybrid and EV combined (~41%).
autos.whyItMatters: The fuel mix is now roughly half alternative, which reshapes powertrain capex, supplier exposure and how strategic buyers assess component targets.

industrials.headline: Q2FY27 preview: soft order inflows and commodity inflation weigh on capital goods
industrials.summary: Ex-L&T inflows for major capital goods firms are estimated at about ₹35,000 crore, roughly 10% lower YoY, while L&T reported about ₹1 trillion including West Asia hydrocarbon wins. Copper, zinc, aluminium and pig iron each rose by double digits QoQ, and EBITDA margins are expected to compress, especially on fixed-price contracts without pass-through clauses.
industrials.whyItMatters: Expect margin-led estimate cuts. In diligence, look closely at contract pass-through terms and order-book quality; a valuation premium relies on execution, not just order intake.

industrials.headline: Power T&D and private capex remain the bright spots
industrials.summary: The same analysis points to a sharply higher power transmission and distribution order book and a revival in private capex across manufacturing, oil & gas, data centres and renewables. GE Vernova's quarterly inflow depends on when a ~$1.5 billion HVDC order is booked.
industrials.whyItMatters: Grid and data-centre themes are where strategic and financial-sponsor interest is likely to concentrate, from transformer and switchgear capacity to cable makers.

aerospace-defence.headline: MoD signs ₹661.5 crore BrahMos fire-control and launcher contract for the Navy
aerospace-defence.summary: The Ministry of Defence signed a ₹661.50 crore contract with BrahMos Aerospace for fire-control systems and launchers for Indian Navy warships, under the Buy (Indian-IDDM) category with at least 68% indigenous content and MSME participation.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Steady IDDM-category awards support the order visibility of listed defence electronics and tier-2 suppliers, which underpins their premium valuations.

aerospace-defence.headline: Airbus delivers 72 jets in September; Q4 now carries the year
aerospace-defence.summary: September deliveries rose to 72 from 57 in August, taking the year-to-date total to 547 (+8% YoY). With a full-year target of about 870, Airbus needs 323 deliveries in October–December. Gross orders were light at 17 and the backlog fell to 9,310 aircraft.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Delivery ramps drive aero-structures and component suppliers, including Indian offset and build-to-print vendors. Any Q4 miss tends to flow through to supplier guidance.

aerospace-defence.headline: Defence order inflows up 19% YoY, adjusted for HAL's high base
aerospace-defence.summary: Q2FY27 defence inflows are estimated at about ₹8,600 crore, up 19% YoY excluding last year's ₹62,300 crore HAL LCA order. Delays persist on QRSAM, P-75I and the next-generation corvettes. HAL expects 12 more GE engines by December.
aerospace-defence.whyItMatters: Programme timing, not demand, is the key swing factor. Watch P-75I and QRSAM finalisation as near-term catalysts for the sector.

regulatory.headline: RBI raises repo rate 25 bps to 5.50%, moves to 'calibrated tightening'
regulatory.summary: The MPC voted unanimously to hike on 7 October; the stance change passed 4–2. FY27 projections are 7.1% real GDP growth and 5.2% CPI inflation, with inflation expected to peak near 6% in Q3 FY27.
regulatory.whyItMatters: Higher rates raise the cost of acquisition finance and vehicle loans. Factor this into LBO debt capacity and into volume sensitivities for auto names.
